subject: Renewal: multi-year protection + upfront credits (proposal and timeline)
messages:
From: Elena Martens <elena@acmeanalytics.com>
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Renewal window and potential multi-year option

Hi Jasmine,

Our renewal for the inference usage contract is coming up in late December. Usage has grown ~2.3x this year and finance is anxious about the vendor price increases we've seen across the stack. Before we kick off a full procurement RFP I wanted to check if Redwood has any multi-year/advance-credit constructs that could:

- lock today's unit rates for 12–36 months,
- offer a staged ramp in consumption credits so we don't overspend early in the term, and
- include a clear exit or usage true-up so our CFO feels comfortable.

Ravi (cc) is our purchasing lead and will own the contractual pieces. Can you share any example structures and a rough timeline for quoting?

Thanks,
Elena
Director, Platform Engineering
Acme Analytics
From: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai
To: Elena Martens <elena@acmeanalytics.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@acmeanalytics.com>
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 11:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal window and potential multi-year option

Elena — thanks for the note and congrats on the growth. We have a couple of commercially proven ways to achieve what you described. High level options (quick summary):

1) Multi-year prepay + ramp credits (recommended for predictable spend)
   - 2–3 year term with an upfront payment covering a discounted token pool.
   - Year 1: conservative credit drawdown assumption; years 2–3: credits increase as you ramp.
   - Built-in quarterly true-ups and a one-time reconciliation at renewal.

2) Annual prepay with auto-price protection add-on
   - Pay annually but add a price-protection rider that limits unit-rate increases to a fixed cap.

3) Reserved capacity (Dedicated) + usage overlay
   - For high-throughput paths we can offer reserved GPU capacity and a separate usage tier.

I'll attach a mock quote that shows example numbers for a 3-year prepay with stepped credit releases. If you want, Marcus (our Director of Sales Strategy) can put together a detailed amortization schedule keyed to your current usage profile.

Next steps I suggest:
- You confirm a target term (2 vs 3 years) and desired price protection level.
- Marcus builds a model and we share the draft commercial term sheet.
- If that looks good, Legal/Procurement can receive a redlineable contract.

Attaching: RI_renewal_quote_v2.pdf (sample numbers + amortization).

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
From: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai
Cc: Elena Martens <elena@acmeanalytics.com>, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 08:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal window and potential multi-year option

Elena / Jasmine — looping in some specifics from our side. Two pragmatic structures we typically propose for customers at Acme's scale: 

A) Hedge + Stage (3-year example)
- Year 1 prepay = 40% of expected 3-year consumption at a ~18% unit discount.
- Year 2 draw release = additional 35% at a ~14% discount.
- Year 3 remaining credits = 25% at a ~10% discount.
- Quarterly true-ups to avoid large final reconciliations; unused credits roll forward within the term but expire at term end.

B) Annual Prepay + Price Cap Rider
- Annual prepay for Year 1 at a 12% discount, with a rider that caps price increases to +5% year-over-year for the length of the rider.

Practical notes:
- We can build a ramp schedule tied to your product release timeline so you don't prepay heavily before the ramp.
- If Acme needs stronger cashflow smoothing, we can convert prepaid dollars into a credit line with scheduled invoicing (adds complexity, requires finance sign-off).

If you share a 12-month usage forecast (token counts or request-rate buckets) we'll model exact costs and show the breakeven vs pay-as-you-go.

Marcus Lin
Director, Sales Strategy | Redwood Inference
From: Elena Martens <elena@acmeanalytics.com>
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@acmeanalytics.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 14:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal window and potential multi-year option

Thanks Marcus — this is helpful. A few follow-ups from Procurement and Finance: 

- Procurement: we need a clear clause for a mid-term scale-up option (ability to convert more spend into credits at a pre-agreed uplift). Can you propose the uplift amount and any limits?
- Finance: requires that unused credits be refundable at a cadence or at least transferable to a new legal entity (we're evaluating an internal restructure). Is transferability something Redwood supports?
- Legal: will want a concise true-up mechanism and a simple termination-for-convenience fee cap.

Can you put those mechanics into a short term-sheet (1–2 pages) so our legal/procurement team can review? If it looks reasonable we will share a procurement window and timeline.

Elena
From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: Elena Martens <elena@acmeanalytics.com>, jasmine_liu@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 16:34:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal window and potential multi-year option

Elena — appreciate the specific asks. Internal confirmation: we can support the following in a short term-sheet and draft:

- Mid-term scale-up: allowed up to 50% of the originally prepaid pool at a fixed uplift of +8% on the then-applicable unit price. Scale-ups will be invoiced and credited into the existing pool.
- Transferability: we can allow an assignment to a related entity subject to creditworthiness review and a small administrative fee (standard carve-outs for change-of-control).
- True-up: quarterly reconciliation with a final term-end reconciliation; unconsumed credits may be refunded at 60% of face value if requested at term-end (this balances cashflow and risk).
- Termination: termination-for-convenience allowed with a fee capped at 20% of remaining prepaid value (to avoid disproportionate churn risk).

I'll convert these bullets into a 2-page commercial term-sheet and circulate early next week. Jasmine — can you confirm the usage profile attachment from Acme when you send the term-sheet?

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Head of Renewals | Redwood Inference
